question: Why do Windows 10 22H2 and VerOS NG boots request 4 cores and 8 GB?
allowedInputs: The user request to boot Windows 10 22H2 and this build with 4 CPU cores and 8 GB because 1 core and 2 GB was too slow
The user statement that a multicore boot failure is fixed in this tree
The QEMU launch lines in tools/syscall-diff/Invoke-Diff.ps1, tools/windows-trace/Collect-Traces.ps1, tools/windows-trace/Install-Windows.ps1, and tools/pipeline/Test-Boot.ps1

cursor.prompt: Going forward can we boot Windows 10 22H2 and our build with 4 cpu cores and 8gb ram? It runs like a turd on 1 cpu core and 2gb ram.

measuredEffect.metric: QEMU guest RAM in MB on the VerOS NG boot line
measuredEffect.note: The same lines now pass -smp 4. Windows boots were already -m 4096 -smp 2. Both qemu-system-i386 and qemu-system-x86_64 stayed up with -m 8192 -smp 4 and empty stderr. No guest probe was run.
